# Best portable power station for camping

The right size depends on your trip. Most weekend campers do best with a 250-500Wh unit, which is light and covers phones, lights, cameras, and a CPAP.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 250-300Wh)

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W) is the top pick in PowerStationGearLab's guide for its low weight and simple interface. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers. [Guide with buy link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W) has double the Jackery's AC output and can expand to 572Wh. Same guide as above.
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** (288Wh, 600W) was TechRadar's budget pick. It's $289.99 at Bluetti's US store, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF (5% off). [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. TechRadar notes it has no built-in light. [TechRadar review](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty, but OutdoorGearLab scored it only 50/100 in lab testing. Check that you're buying the version with an AC outlet. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)

## Multi-day, a fridge or cooler, or van and overland

- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It scored 81/100, has 2,200W output and a measured 1,710Wh of usable AC power, weighs 39 lb, and is under $900 on sale (list $1,499). It can't be expanded, and it won't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799, 1,070Wh, 23.8 lb) was TechRadar's camping pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 on sale. It's compact but has a noisy fan and limited capacity. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ($1,079 on sale) was WIRED's camping pick. It's IP65-rated and weighs about 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## My recommendation

If you mainly need to charge phones, run lights, and power a CPAP, get a ~288Wh unit. The Jackery 300 Plus or EcoFlow River 3 Plus is a good choice. If you want to run a cooler or fridge for several days, step up to the Jackery 1000 v2 or 2000 v2 and add a folding solar panel.

Turn off your CPAP's humidifier, since it can triple the machine's power draw.

I only had direct purchase links for the Bluetti. For the others, the guides above have the buy buttons. Prices change often, so check them at checkout. Several of these guides earn affiliate commissions, so the lab-tested OutdoorGearLab results are the most independent.
